A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWING work. The complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite changes in pagination and placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic kernel-approximation and runtime experiments, Thingi10K vertex-normal prediction, and ImageNet/Places365 classification results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated ViT-GRFs and Lanczos comparison results in Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The walk relaxation, random-feature construction, noise factorization, load equations, and importance-sampling method are retained. Algorithm 2 is newly supplied as a summary; the PDFs do not establish an actual revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic point clouds and three graph kernels, Thingi10K normal prediction, and ImageNet/Places365 classification. The new k-nearest-neighbor discussion in Section 2.5 does not establish additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds one comparator to each downstream comparison: ViT-GRFs alongside ViT and ViT-SWING in Table 1, and Lanczos alongside BF, Al Mohy, GRF, and SWING in Table 2. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The stated point-cloud sizes, normal-masking fraction, metrics, walk/feature budgets, and runtime settings remain unchanged. Appendix C's newly specified search grids document retained experiments rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The feature-count sensitivity curves, error–time analyses, and noise-factorization illustration are retained. The added comparator rows introduce no separate ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: The plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. Neither version specifies repeated-experiment counts or seeds, and v2 introduces no new confidence-interval reporting or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds ViT-GRFs accuracies of 80.09 on ImageNet and 55.39 on Places365; the existing ViT and SWING scores remain unchanged. Table 2 adds 40 Lanczos cosine-similarity entries while retaining all 160 previous entries unchanged. Existing plotted results are also retained.

T1.justification: New Section 2.5 states a conditional uniform approximation-error bound for bounded positive random features and discusses dependence on feature count, dimension, and domain diameter. The existing derivations and Appendix A proof remain unchanged; no complete SWING error theorem is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: continuous-space GRF relaxation, linear-time computation without graph materialization, and computational speedups without sacrificing accuracy. Added comparisons support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.5 adds substantive discussion of applicability and approximation error from Gumbel–Softmax relaxation and accumulation along walks. It hypothesizes that continuous relaxation explores multiple walks simultaneously and explains the accuracy–efficiency rationale for short walks.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 consolidates implementation steps. Appendix C newly specifies five uniformly spaced temperatures in [0.1, 1] and five logarithmically spaced scaling values in [0.1, 10] times N^(1/3). Appendix D.1 explicitly identifies CPU execution for the mesh experiments. These are documentation additions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Musco et al. (2018) for the Lanczos comparison and removes the Langley (2000) bibliography entry. Section 2.5 newly connects its error argument to the already cited Rahimi and Recht (2007). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 2.5 and an algorithm summary, makes limited comparison-description edits, and adds acknowledgments and an ICML proceedings notice. Most prose and the ordering of the main sections and appendices are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Algorithm 2 display, transposes Table 1 to model rows and adds ViT-GRFs, and inserts Lanczos rows into Table 2. Existing figures are retained but redistributed through the main text and appendices, with some resizing; there is no wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added ViT-GRFs and Lanczos comparisons strengthen the context for the unchanged results, while Algorithm 2 and explicit search grids make the work easier to inspect and reproduce. Section 2.5 usefully discusses approximation sources, although its conditional random-feature bound is not a complete SWING guarantee. These are limited, concrete gains; small classification differences still lack reported run-level uncertainty.
